the update has rank at most r even though W is full rank. Demonstration:
```python
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
d_out, d_in, r, alpha = 12, 20, 4, 8
W = rng.normal(size=(d_out, d_in)); A = rng.normal(size=(r, d_in)) * 0.1; B = rng.normal(size=(d_out, r)) * 0.1
x = rng.normal(size=(5, d_in))
Wm = merge_lora(W, A, B, alpha, r)
assert np.allclose(x @ Wm.T, lora_forward(x, W, A, B, alpha, r), atol=1e-10)
assert np.linalg.matrix_rank(Wm - W, tol=1e-9) == r  # <= r in general; == r for random A, B
```

reasons: Numbers verified, but the Euclidean statement is wrong for the question's own example.

issues.claim: So switching to Euclidean does not address a norm effect; normalising does.
issues.problem: Euclidean distance is norm-sensitive and in the example ranks [2, 0, 1] (squared distances 0.45, 81.8, 163.8 vs the long vector [10,10]), so it demotes the long vector; it just differs from cosine by penalising any norm mismatch (including short, correct documents) instead of ignoring norm.
issues.replacement: So switching to Euclidean does not reproduce cosine: it penalises any norm mismatch with the query (here it ranks [0.5, 0.45], then [10, 0], then [10, 10], whereas cosine ranks [10, 10] second), so it can demote the long vectors but also demotes legitimate documents whose norm differs from the query's; normalising is the targeted fix.

issues.claim: If every vector is L2-normalised, |a-b|^2 = 2 - 2cos, so cosine, dot product and Euclidean distance produce identical rankings
issues.problem: Sufficient but not necessary: equal document norms already make all three rankings identical for a given query.
issues.replacement: If every vector is L2-normalised (or, for a fixed query, all documents merely share one norm), |a-b|^2 = 2 - 2cos up to constants, so cosine, dot product and Euclidean distance produce identical rankings

issues.problem: The threshold's own trade-off (what raising or lowering overlap >= threshold does) is not stated although the question asks for it.
